How to Check OpenCode Token Usage

Run opencode stats --project . --days 7 --cost to see the current project’s token and cost report. For a single CLI run, save the output of opencode run --format json and check the step_finish records. Read input and cache counts separately, and use your provider’s usage dashboard to verify charges.

  1. Show project or model totals
  2. Read a JSON lines run log
  3. Check costs or a usage limit
  4. Compare the measured token counts

Which usage number do you need?

Show statsRead logCheck provider

Show token usage by project and model

From the project directory, run these commands in OpenCode 2. Check available flags with opencode stats --help if you use an older release.

opencode stats --project . --days 7 --cost
opencode stats --project . --days 7 --models
opencode stats --project . --days 7 --full --json

The last command returns the aggregate as JSON. Use --all in place of --days 7 to compare lifetime data in the same store. An empty report can mean the current project, date range or server differs from the one you used. Confirm the project and session first.

Read token counts from an OpenCode run log

Run a task you are comfortable repeating and redirect its JSON lines output to a file. Each completed model step can produce a step_finish record. Save the file privately because the full log can contain text, tool output and project details.

opencode run --format json "Explain the test command in this project." > run.ndjson
Choose an OpenCode JSON lines log.

The file stays in your browser. The reader sums complete step records, reports skipped rows and counts each identified session once. Download an example log. It should report 3 steps, 2 sessions, 754 input, 11 output and 1,451 cache-read tokens.

For a terminal check with jq installed, select the usage values directly.

jq -c 'select(.type == "step_finish") | .part.tokens' run.ndjson

Check cost, cache use and provider limits

Compare input, output, reasoning and cache fields separately. In our Ollama test, cached input appeared in cache.read while remaining input appeared in input. Reading only input made the follow-up look much smaller than the combined counts. Other providers can report categories differently.

Use your provider’s own usage dashboard for charges and included allowances. A locally reported cost of zero in this test reflects the local provider run. It does not measure the cost of the computer or the electricity it used. For a subscription cap, see OpenCode Go limits and reset times.

First prompt72434

We used OpenCode 2.4.1 with Ollama 0.40.18 and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M in a temporary macOS arm64 project. The project’s aggregate matched the sum of all three steps. A separate project with a different initial commit returned no sessions. The counts apply to these three requests on one local runner, with no hosted billing test. Download the measured totals.

See the OpenCode CLI reference for the report flags. To set up the local model first, follow the OpenCode first-run tutorial.
